items.title: Tauri app entry: builder, plugins, managed state, command registry, launch args
items.rationale: Composition root for every area (lib.rs:190-430). Keep the structure; prune registrations/state of removed modules (AI BYOK per ADR-004, IDE tools per ADR-002/10.2) as those areas delete them, drop the unused pty_has_foreground_job command, rename the `__terax_notify` argv subcommand (lib.rs:170, hook marker, F0:10) and the control-server log text (lib.rs:244). Settings-window event `terax:settings-tab` (lib.rs:103) is internal IPC.
items.risks: Merge hotspot: every removal PR edits the generate_handler! list; each removal PR should touch only its own lines.

items.title: PTY output transport v2: hub thread, terax-pty URI scheme, admission gate, wire framing, flow control
items.rationale: High-value, well-tested core (ADR-003, 5.10:1, 10.1:7: do not rewrite the PTY transport). The `terax-pty` scheme name is a per-webview registration (lib.rs:218) and cannot collide with an installed Terax; rename only on touch.
couplings: build-identity (CSP/capabilities must allow the terax-pty origin)
items.risks: A scheme rename would need coordinated CSP + frontend + smoke harness changes; not worth it.

items.title: PTY session lifecycle and Tauri commands (pty_open/write/resize/close, colors, foreground, diagnostics)
items.rationale: Keep lifecycle (TER-001, TER-005, 6.5:1). pty_open (mod.rs:172-185) only takes cols/rows/cwd/workspace/blocks/shell/pane_id/presentation/colors: extend it with a launch spec (program+args, env overrides, WSL distro, cwd fallback) for profiles (PRO-002, PRO-003, PRO-006, F3:3) and typed errors for missing executable/cwd/distro (PRO-010, 13.2:12, 13.5:7). Emit a shell-ready signal (8.4:6). Remove unused pty_has_foreground_job (mod.rs:384, no frontend caller). Event names `terax:agent-signal`/`terax:terminal-notification` (session.rs:22-23) are internal.
items.risks: Accepting arbitrary executables/env over IPC widens the attack surface vs today's allowlist (shell_init.rs:115-129); needs a policy decision.

items.title: Shell command builder: detection, enumeration, env injection, integration script install (incl. WSL)
items.rationale: Phase 0: writes integration scripts to ~/.cache/terax/shell-integration (shell_init.rs:449,912) and WSL $HOME/.cache/terax (shell_init.rs:857,900), shared with and overwritten by an installed Terax; injects TERAX_* env vars (shell_init.rs:195-219,394,772,778) read by Terax tooling (F0:10, identity:1, 13.2:21). Then: launch spec for profiles (PRO-002, F3:3), replace the enumerated-shell allowlist (115-129), add WSL distros and more shells to discovery (F3:6, PRO-006), PowerShell -NoProfile option (7.3).
items.risks: Changing the cache dir/env names must be atomic with the scripts and the CLI or integration silently breaks.

items.title: Shell integration scripts (bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell) and their tests
items.rationale: Keep OSC 7/133 behaviour (7.3, 5.10:1). Phase 0: guard variable __TERAX_HOOKS_LOADED (bashrc.bash:10, profile.ps1:6, init.fish) and TERAX_CLI/TERAX_BLOCKS/TERAX_TERMINAL/TERAX_USER_ZDOTDIR plus the `terax` shell function (profile.ps1:10) must use lut names (F0:10). Internal _terax_* function names rename on touch only.
items.risks: Script tests (bashrc.test.bash, zshrc.test.py, init.test.fish) are not wired into any package script/CI; run manually.

items.title: In-stream agent detection: OSC 133/9/99/777 parsing, Terax hook marker, agent status signals
items.rationale: Keep (AGT-001, AGT-004). Phase 0: TERAX_MARKER `notify;Terax;` (agent_detect.rs:35,421) is the hook marker emitted by `<exe> __terax_notify` (lib.rs:170); it must become lut-specific so Terax hooks running inside lut panes (and vice versa) are not misattributed (F0:10, 13.2:21).
items.risks: Marker must change together with the emitter in agent.rs (agents area).

items.title: Process helpers: captured child processes, Windows Job Object, RSS, hide_console
items.rationale: Shared plumbing used by pty (session.rs, pty_diagnostics mod.rs:513), git/process.rs, lsp/session.rs, workspace.rs, shell/. Job Object kill-on-close is the Windows orphan guard (13.3:1). Thread names terax-cap-* are internal.
items.risks: Callers shrink as ide-tools/ai are removed; re-check for dead code afterwards.

items.title: Non-PTY shell execution (one-shot commands, persistent shell sessions, background processes) for AI tools
items.rationale: Only callers are the BYOK AI agent tools (src/modules/ai/lib/native.ts) and editor external formatting (src/modules/editor/lib/externalFormat.ts); lut retires integrated AI (ADR-004) and the IDE editor (ADR-002, 10.2). Remove once those consumers are gone.

items.title: Raw IPC request body helper
items.rationale: Only used by net.rs and ai_sessions.rs (AI BYOK, ADR-004). Remove with the AI modules.
items.risks: Trivial to restore if a future command needs raw bodies.

items.title: Shell history index (zsh/bash/fish histfiles + PATH) for command suggestions
items.rationale: User decision 3 (analysis/decisions.md): only serves block-mode suggestions and the palette history mode, both removed with blocks mode. (Analyst: Used only by terminal block-mode suggestions (src/modules/terminal/block/lib/history.ts). Not required by the proposal; keep/drop depends on whether lut keeps block mode/autosuggest (terminal area decision). Reads user histfiles only; no identity impact.)
items.risks: No PowerShell history support, so limited value on lut's first target (Windows 11).

items.title: Tokio runtime sizing for commands
items.rationale: Generic and small; keeps idle footprint low (13.4:5).

items.title: Window presentation state (live resize, occlusion/sleep) for renderers
items.rationale: Renderer behaviour, not visual design; feeds terminal/ghostty/windowPresentation.ts (ADR-003, 5.4:4). Revisit for multi-window (F7:1).

items.title: Window backdrop (Mica / NSVisualEffectView) commands
items.rationale: User decision 16 (analysis/decisions.md): window vibrancy is a kept personalisation feature. (Analyst: Pure visual capability; whether lut uses a translucent backdrop is part of the user's UI design (ADR-002). Leave untouched until the design decides; then keep or remove.)

items.title: Real-webview PTY transport smoke/perf harness (macOS only)
items.rationale: Valuable baseline for 13.4:2/13.4:3 and F0:11, but run.py refuses non-Darwin hosts and builds a temp app with bundle id app.crynta.terax.pty-smoke-*. Port to Windows 11, use lut identifiers, drop driver-old.ts (benchmarks the removed per-terminal channel transport).
items.risks: Uses tauri build --debug; slow; needs WebView2 automation on Windows.

items.title: IPC profiling harness for fs/lsp/AI-session commands (macOS only)
items.rationale: User decision 2 (analysis/decisions.md): fs/lsp stay; drop only the AI-session parts of the harness when AI is removed. (Analyst: Exercises fs_grep/fs_search/lsp_host_pid/AI sessions (smoke.ts:1-90), all owned by removed areas (ADR-004, ADR-002); macOS only (run.py:18).)

items.title: Shared integration-test helpers
items.rationale: Used by tests/fs_search.rs and tests/git_operations.rs (other areas); remove only when its last user goes.

notes: Phase 0 identity collisions found here: ~/.cache/terax/shell-integration (and WSL $HOME/.cache/terax) shared and overwritten by both apps; TERAX_* env vars injected into children and read by terax-cli; __TERAX_HOOKS_LOADED guard; OSC 777 marker notify;Terax; plus the `__terax_notify` argv subcommand. The terax-pty URI scheme and thread names do NOT collide. pty_has_foreground_job has no frontend caller.
